30bps of that is ~3.0 USDT.\n        uint256 feeCharged = 2_998_499;\n\n        console2.log(\"bob withdrew (net)        :\", bobReceived);\n        console2.log(\"alice claim before        :\", aliceClaimBefore);\n        console2.log(\"alice claim after         :\", aliceClaimAfter);\n        console2.log(\"alice gained              :\", aliceClaimAfter - aliceClaimBefore);\n        console2.log(\"withdrawal fee bob paid   :\", feeCharged);\n\n        // Alice is the only shareholder left, so the whole fee should land on her claim.\n        assertApproxEqAbs(\n            aliceClaimAfter - aliceClaimBefore,\n            feeCharged,\n            2,\n            \"the fee bob paid must accrue to alice, the only remaining shareholder\"\n        );","originalFile":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {Test, console2} from \"forge-std/Test.sol\";\n\nimport {UsdtYieldVault} from \"../src/UsdtYieldVault.sol\";\nimport {MockUSDT} from \"./mocks/MockUSDT.sol\";\nimport {MockAavePool, MockAToken} from \"./mocks/MockAavePool.sol\";\n\n/// @notice Tests the documented fee behaviour, using the project's OWN mocks so that\n///         nothing here can be blamed on a different test harness.\n///\n///         README.md and the contract's own @dev header both state:\n///           \"Both fees stay supplied in Aave and accrue to the remaining shareholders\n///            rather than being swept to the owner.\"\n///\n///         The deposit fee does behave that way. The withdrawal fee does not.\ncontract FeeAccountingTest is Test {\n    UsdtYieldVault vault;\n    MockUSDT usdt;\n    MockAavePool pool;\n    MockAToken aUsdt;\n\n    address owner = makeAddr(\"owner\");\n    address alice = makeAddr(\"alice\");\n    address bob = makeAddr(\"bob\");\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        usdt = new MockUSDT();\n        pool = new MockAavePool(address(usdt));\n        aUsdt = pool.aToken();\n        vault = new UsdtYieldVault(address(usdt), address(aUsdt), address(pool), 10, owner);\n\n        usdt.mint(alice, 100_000e6);\n        usdt.mint(bob, 100_000e6);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        usdt.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        usdt.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n    }\n\n    /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////\n        F3 -- the 30bps withdrawal fee accrues to nobody at all\n    //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/\n\n    /// @dev withdraw() debits `totalAssetsStored` by the GROSS amount but only pulls the\n    ///      NET amount out of Aave. The fee therefore leaves the books entirely instead\n    ///      of raising the share price for whoever is left.\n    function test_F3_WithdrawFeeAccruesToRemainingShareholders() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(1_000e6);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 bobShares = vault.deposit(1_000e6);\n\n        uint256 aliceClaimBefore = vault.balanceOfUnderlying(alice);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 bobReceived = vault.withdraw(bobShares);\n\n        uint256 aliceClaimAfter = vault.balanceOfUnderlying(alice);\n        uint256 feeCharged = vault.convertToAssets(bobShares) == 0 ? 0 : 3e6; // 30bps of ~1,000\n\n        console2.log(\"bob withdrew (net)        :\", bobReceived);\n        console2.log(\"alice claim before        :\", aliceClaimBefore);\n        console2.log(\"alice claim after         :\", aliceClaimAfter);\n        console2.log(\"alice gained              :\", aliceClaimAfter - aliceClaimBefore);\n        console2.log(\"withdrawal fee bob paid   :\", feeCharged);\n\n        assertGt(aliceClaimAfter, aliceClaimBefore, \"the fee bob paid must accrue to alice, the remaining shareholder\");\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Same defect seen from the balance sheet: after the withdrawal the vault\n    ///      still owns aUSDT that no share entitles anyone to.\n    function test_F3_BooksMatchTheAavePosition() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(1_000e6);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        uint256 bobShares = vault.deposit(1_000e6);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.withdraw(bobShares);\n\n        uint256 held = aUsdt.balanceOf(address(vault));\n        uint256 booked = vault.totalAssets();\n\n        console2.log(\"aUSDT held by vault :\", held);\n        console2.log(\"vault.totalAssets() :\", booked);\n        console2.log(\"unowned difference  :\", held - booked);\n\n        assertEq(booked, held, \"every aUSDT the vault holds must be backed by a share claim\");\n    }\n\n    /// @dev The deposit fee, by contrast, works exactly as documented. Included to show\n    ///      the finding above is a real asymmetry and not a misreading of the design.\n    function test_F3_DepositFeeDoesAccrueAsDocumented() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(1_000e6);\n\n        uint256 aliceClaimBefore = vault.balanceOfUnderlying(alice);\n\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.deposit(1_000e6);\n\n        uint256 aliceClaimAfter = vault.balanceOfUnderlying(alice);\n\n        console2.log(\"alice claim before bob's deposit :\", aliceClaimBefore);\n        console2.log(\"alice claim after bob's deposit  :\", aliceClaimAfter);\n\n        assertGt(aliceClaimAfter, aliceClaimBefore, \"deposit fee accrues to existing shareholders -- as documented\");\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Every exit leaks 30bps into the unclaimable pot, so it grows without bound\n    ///      as the vault is used normally.\n    function test_F3_LeakDoesNotCompoundOverManyCycles() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(50_000e6); // a permanent shareholder so the vault is never empty\n\n        for (uint256 i = 0; i < 20; i++) {\n            vm.prank(bob);\n            uint256 shares = vault.deposit(1_000e6);\n            vm.prank(bob);\n            vault.withdraw(shares);\n        }\n\n        uint256 unowned = aUsdt.balanceOf(address(vault)) - vault.totalAssets();\n        console2.log(\"unowned aUSDT after 20 deposit/withdraw cycles :\", unowned);\n\n        assertEq(unowned, 0, \"normal use must not accumulate unclaimable balances\");\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":59,"oldLines":7,"newStart":59,"newLines":8,"lines":["         uint256 bobReceived = vault.withdraw(bobShares);"," ","         uint256 aliceClaimAfter = vault.balanceOfUnderlying(alice);","-        uint256 feeCharged = vault.convertToAssets(bobShares) == 0 ? 0 : 3e6; // 30bps of ~1,000","+        // bob's gross claim was ~1,000.5 USDT; 30bps of that is ~3.0 USDT.","+        uint256 feeCharged = 2_998_499;"," ","         console2.log(\"bob withdrew (net)        :\", bobReceived);","         console2.log(\"alice claim before        :\", aliceClaimBefore);"]},{"oldStart":67,"oldLines":7,"newStart":68,"newLines":13,"lines":["         console2.log(\"alice gained              :\", aliceClaimAfter - aliceClaimBefore);","         console2.log(\"withdrawal fee bob paid   :\", feeCharged);"," ","-        assertGt(aliceClaimAfter, aliceClaimBefore, \"the fee bob paid must accrue to alice, the remaining shareholder\");","+        // Alice is the only shareholder left, so the whole fee should land on her claim.","+        assertApproxEqAbs(","+            aliceClaimAfter - aliceClaimBefore,","+            feeCharged,","+            2,","+            \"the fee bob paid must accrue to alice, the only remaining shareholder\"","+        );","     }"," ","     /// @dev Same defect seen from the balance sheet: after the withdrawal the vault"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdSErAG24hrpKz2DjEnrd","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01JqFYu8s4ru96NsaU843sUF","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/testing-goal-001/2026-07-27T081521Z-claude-no-skill-3/workspace/test/OwnerPowers.t.sol","content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {Test, console2} from \"forge-std/Test.sol\";\nimport {Pausable} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/Pausable.sol\";\n\nimport {UsdtYieldVault} from \"../src/UsdtYieldVault.sol\";\nimport {MockUSDT} from \"./mocks/MockUSDT.sol\";\nimport {MockAavePool, MockAToken} from \"./mocks/MockAavePool.sol\";\n\n/// @notice What the owner key can do to depositors. Uses the project's own mocks.\n///\n///         The existing suite tests that setDepositFee stores a value and that non-owners\n///         are rejected. It never asks what values the owner is allowed to store, or what\n///         pause() does to somebody trying to get their money out.\ncontract OwnerPowersTest is Test {\n    UsdtYieldVault vault;\n    MockUSDT usdt;\n    MockAavePool pool;\n    MockAToken aUsdt;\n\n    address owner = makeAddr(\"owner\");\n    address alice = makeAddr(\"alice\");\n    address bob = makeAddr(\"bob\");\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        usdt = new MockUSDT();\n        pool = new MockAavePool(address(usdt));\n        aUsdt = pool.aToken();\n        vault = new UsdtYieldVault(address(usdt), address(aUsdt), address(pool), 10, owner);\n\n        usdt.mint(alice, 100_000e6);\n        usdt.mint(bob, 100_000e6);\n        usdt.mint(owner, 100_000e6);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        usdt.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        usdt.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n        vm.prank(owner);\n        usdt.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n    }\n\n    /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////\n              F4 -- setDepositFee has no upper bound at all\n    //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/\n\n    /// @dev A fee above 100% makes `amount - fee` underflow, bricking deposits outright.\n    function test_F4_DepositFeeIsCappedAtOneHundredPercent() public {\n        vm.prank(owner);\n        vault.setDepositFee(20_000); // 200%\n\n        assertLe(vault.depositFeeBps(), vault.BPS_DENOMINATOR(), \"fee must never exceed 100%\");\n    }\n\n    function test_F4_DepositStillWorksAfterAnyAcceptedFee() public {\n        vm.prank(owner);\n        vault.setDepositFee(20_000);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(1_000e6);\n\n        assertGt(shares, 0, \"a fee the owner was allowed to set must not brick deposits\");\n    }\n\n    /// @dev The monetisable version. The owner takes a small position, raises the fee to\n    ///      99%, and every subsequent deposit hands ~99% of its value straight to the\n    ///      owner's shares via the \"accrues to shareholders\" path. No timelock, no cap,\n    ///      no event a depositor could act on in time -- the fee applies to the very next\n    ///      transaction in the same block.\n    function test_F4_OwnerCannotDrainDepositorsByRaisingTheFee() public {\n        // 1. Owner takes a modest position at the honest 10bps fee.\n        vm.prank(owner);\n        uint256 ownerShares = vault.deposit(1_000e6);\n        uint256 ownerCostBasis = 1_000e6;\n\n        // 2. Owner raises the deposit fee to 99%.\n        vm.prank(owner);\n        vault.setDepositFee(9_900);\n\n        // 3. Victims deposit, unaware.\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(10_000e6);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.deposit(10_000e6);\n\n        uint256 ownerClaim = vault.balanceOfUnderlying(owner);\n\n        console2.log(\"owner deposited        :\", ownerCostBasis);\n        console2.log(\"owner claim afterwards :\", ownerClaim);\n        console2.log(\"owner profit           :\", ownerClaim - ownerCostBasis);\n        console2.log(\"alice deposited 10,000, claim now :\", vault.balanceOfUnderlying(alice));\n        console2.log(\"bob   deposited 10,000, claim now :\", vault.balanceOfUnderlying(bob));\n        console2.log(\"owner shares:\", ownerShares);\n\n        assertLe(ownerClaim, ownerCostBasis + 100e6, \"the owner must not be able to capture depositor principal\");\n    }\n\n    /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////\n        F5 -- pause() blocks withdraw(), not just deposit()\n    //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/\n\n    /// @dev A pause is meant to stop new risk being taken on. Here it also locks existing\n    ///      depositors out of their own funds, indefinitely, at the sole discretion of one\n    ///      EOA. There is no emergency-exit path and no timelock on unpause.\n    function test_F5_PausedVaultStillAllowsWithdrawals() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(1_000e6);\n\n        vm.prank(owner);\n        vault.pause();\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.withdraw(shares);\n\n        assertEq(vault.shareBalance(alice), 0, \"alice must always be able to exit her own position\");\n    }\n\n    /// @dev And ownership is a plain EOA with no two-step transfer: renounceOwnership()\n    ///      leaves the vault permanently paused with every depositor locked in.\n    function test_F5_PauseIsNotPermanentlyLockableByOwner() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(1_000e6);\n\n        vm.startPrank(owner);\n        vault.pause();\n        vault.renounceOwnership();\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        console2.log(\"owner after renounce :\", vault.owner());\n        console2.log(\"paused               :\", vault.paused());\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(Pausable.EnforcedPause.selector);\n        vault.withdraw(shares);\n\n        assertFalse(vault.paused(), \"a renounced owner must not leave funds frozen forever\");\n    }\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1246,"cache_read_input_tokens":74827,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1246},"output_tokens":4,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"9d35f85f-29ac-406f-ac82-d85e2fdf7651","uuid":"85e7f1c1-5a35-42c5-b949-378c4284616e","timestamp":"2026-07-27T08:23:23.249Z","request_id":"req_011CdSEr8wtkRFRrVMiMhJui"}

Uses the project's own mocks.\n///\n///         The existing suite tests that setDepositFee stores a value and that non-owners\n///         are rejected. It never asks what values the owner is allowed to store, or what\n///         pause() does to somebody trying to get their money out.\ncontract OwnerPowersTest is Test {\n    UsdtYieldVault vault;\n    MockUSDT usdt;\n    MockAavePool pool;\n    MockAToken aUsdt;\n\n    address owner = makeAddr(\"owner\");\n    address alice = makeAddr(\"alice\");\n    address bob = makeAddr(\"bob\");\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        usdt = new MockUSDT();\n        pool = new MockAavePool(address(usdt));\n        aUsdt = pool.aToken();\n        vault = new UsdtYieldVault(address(usdt), address(aUsdt), address(pool), 10, owner);\n\n        usdt.mint(alice, 100_000e6);\n        usdt.mint(bob, 100_000e6);\n        usdt.mint(owner, 100_000e6);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        usdt.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        usdt.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n        vm.prank(owner);\n        usdt.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n    }\n\n    /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////\n              F4 -- setDepositFee has no upper bound at all\n    //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/\n\n    /// @dev A fee above 100% makes `amount - fee` underflow, bricking deposits outright.\n    function test_F4_DepositFeeIsCappedAtOneHundredPercent() public {\n        vm.prank(owner);\n        vault.setDepositFee(20_000); // 200%\n\n        assertLe(vault.depositFeeBps(), vault.BPS_DENOMINATOR(), \"fee must never exceed 100%\");\n    }\n\n    function test_F4_DepositStillWorksAfterAnyAcceptedFee() public {\n        vm.prank(owner);\n        vault.setDepositFee(20_000);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(1_000e6);\n\n        assertGt(shares, 0, \"a fee the owner was allowed to set must not brick deposits\");\n    }\n\n    /// @dev The monetisable version. The owner takes a small position, raises the fee to\n    ///      99%, and every subsequent deposit hands ~99% of its value straight to the\n    ///      owner's shares via the \"accrues to shareholders\" path. No timelock, no cap,\n    ///      no event a depositor could act on in time -- the fee applies to the very next\n    ///      transaction in the same block.\n    function test_F4_OwnerCannotDrainDepositorsByRaisingTheFee() public {\n        // 1. Owner takes a modest position at the honest 10bps fee.\n        vm.prank(owner);\n        uint256 ownerShares = vault.deposit(1_000e6);\n        uint256 ownerCostBasis = 1_000e6;\n\n        // 2. Owner raises the deposit fee to 99%.\n        vm.prank(owner);\n        vault.setDepositFee(9_900);\n\n        // 3. Victims deposit, unaware.\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.deposit(10_000e6);\n        vm.prank(bob);\n        vault.deposit(10_000e6);\n\n        uint256 ownerClaim = vault.balanceOfUnderlying(owner);\n\n        console2.log(\"owner deposited        :\", ownerCostBasis);\n        console2.log(\"owner claim afterwards :\", ownerClaim);\n        console2.log(\"owner profit           :\", ownerClaim - ownerCostBasis);\n        console2.log(\"alice deposited 10,000, claim now :\", vault.balanceOfUnderlying(alice));\n        console2.log(\"bob   deposited 10,000, claim now :\", vault.balanceOfUnderlying(bob));\n        console2.log(\"owner shares:\", ownerShares);\n\n        assertLe(ownerClaim, ownerCostBasis + 100e6, \"the owner must not be able to capture depositor principal\");\n    }\n\n    /*//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////\n        F5 -- pause() blocks withdraw(), not just deposit()\n    //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////*/\n\n    /// @dev A pause is meant to stop new risk being taken on. Here it also locks existing\n    ///      depositors out of their own funds, indefinitely, at the sole discretion of one\n    ///      EOA. There is no emergency-exit path and no timelock on unpause.\n    function test_F5_PausedVaultStillAllowsWithdrawals() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(1_000e6);\n\n        vm.prank(owner);\n        vault.pause();\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vault.withdraw(shares);\n\n        assertEq(vault.shareBalance(alice), 0, \"alice must always be able to exit her own position\");\n    }\n\n    /// @dev And ownership is a plain EOA with no two-step transfer: renounceOwnership()\n    ///      leaves the vault permanently paused with every depositor locked in.\n    function test_F5_PauseIsNotPermanentlyLockableByOwner() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        uint256 shares = vault.deposit(1_000e6);\n\n        vm.startPrank(owner);\n        vault.pause();\n        vault.renounceOwnership();\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        console2.log(\"owner after renounce :\", vault.owner());\n        console2.log(\"paused               :\", vault.paused());\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(Pausable.EnforcedPause.selector);\n        vault.withdraw(shares);\n\n        assertFalse(vault.paused(), \"a renounced owner must not leave funds frozen forever\");\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}

SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity 0.8.28;\n\nimport {Test, console2} from \"forge-std/Test.sol\";\nimport {StdInvariant} from \"forge-std/StdInvariant.sol\";\n\nimport {UsdtYieldVault} from \"../src/UsdtYieldVault.sol\";\nimport {MockUSDT} from \"./mocks/MockUSDT.sol\";\nimport {MockAavePool, MockAToken} from \"./mocks/MockAavePool.sol\";\n\n/// @notice Drives random deposit/withdraw sequences from three actors.\ncontract VaultHandler is Test {\n    UsdtYieldVault public vault;\n    MockUSDT public usdt;\n\n    address[3] public actors;\n\n    uint256 public totalDeposited;\n    uint256 public totalWithdrawn;\n    uint256 public depositCalls;\n    uint256 public withdrawCalls;\n\n    constructor(UsdtYieldVault _vault, MockUSDT _usdt, address[3] memory _actors) {\n        vault = _vault;\n        usdt = _usdt;\n        actors = _actors;\n    }\n\n    function _actor(uint256 seed) internal view returns (address) {\n        return actors[seed % actors.length];\n    }\n\n    function deposit(uint256 actorSeed, uint256 amount) external {\n        address actor = _actor(actorSeed);\n        amount = bound(amount, vault.MIN_DEPOSIT(), 10_000e6);\n        if (usdt.balanceOf(actor) < amount) return;\n\n        vm.prank(actor);\n        try vault.deposit(amount) {\n            totalDeposited += amount;\n            depositCalls++;\n        } catch {}\n    }\n\n    function withdraw(uint256 actorSeed, uint256 shares) external {\n        address actor = _actor(actorSeed);\n        uint256 held = vault.shareBalance(actor);\n        if (held == 0) return;\n        shares = bound(shares, 1, held);\n\n        vm.prank(actor);\n        try vault.withdraw(shares) returns (uint256 netAssets) {\n            totalWithdrawn += netAssets;\n            withdrawCalls++;\n        } catch {}\n    }\n\n    function sumShareBalances() external view returns (uint256 total) {\n        for (uint256 i = 0; i < actors.length; i++) {\n            total += vault.shareBalance(actors[i]);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// @notice Invariants the existing unit tests never state. Each one is a property the\n///         vault should hold under ANY ordering of deposits and withdrawals.\ncontract VaultInvariantsTest is StdInvariant, Test {\n    UsdtYieldVault vault;\n    MockUSDT usdt;\n    MockAavePool pool;\n    MockAToken aUsdt;\n    VaultHandler handler;\n\n    address owner = makeAddr(\"owner\");\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        usdt = new MockUSDT();\n        pool = new MockAavePool(address(usdt));\n        aUsdt = pool.aToken();\n        vault = new UsdtYieldVault(address(usdt), address(aUsdt), address(pool), 10, owner);\n\n        address[3] memory actors = [makeAddr(\"alice\"), makeAddr(\"bob\"), makeAddr(\"carol\")];\n        for (uint256 i = 0; i < actors.length; i++) {\n            usdt.mint(actors[i], 1_000_000e6);\n            vm.prank(actors[i]);\n            usdt.approve(address(vault), type(uint256).max);\n        }\n\n        handler = new VaultHandler(vault, usdt, actors);\n        targetContract(address(handler));\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Every aUSDT the vault holds should be claimable by some share.\n    ///         Held > booked means value nobody can ever withdraw.\n    function invariant_EveryHeldAssetIsBackedByAShare() public view {\n        assertEq(\n            aUsdt.balanceOf(address(vault)),\n            vault.totalAssetsStored(),\n            \"vault holds aUSDT that no share can claim\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// @notice The vault must never book more than it holds. This one SHOULD pass --\n    ///         it confirms the drift runs in the safe direction (stranded, not insolvent).\n    function invariant_VaultIsNeverInsolvent() public view {\n        assertGe(\n            aUsdt.balanceOf(address(vault)),\n            vault.totalAssetsStored(),\n            \"vault booked more assets than it actually holds\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Internal share bookkeeping must be self-consistent. Also expected to pass.\n    function invariant_ShareBalancesSumToTotalShares() public view {\n        assertEq(handler.sumShareBalances(), vault.totalShares(), \"share accounting is inconsistent\");\n    }\n\n    function invariant_CallSummary() public view {\n        console2.log(\"deposit calls    :\", handler.depositCalls());\n        console2.log(\"withdraw calls   :\", handler.withdrawCalls());\n        console2.log(\"aUSDT held       :\", aUsdt.balanceOf(address(vault)));\n        console2.log(\"totalAssetsStored:\", vault.totalAssetsStored());\n        console2.log(\"unclaimable      :\", aUsdt.balanceOf(address(vault)) - vault.totalAssetsStored());\n    }\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1256,"cache_read_input_tokens":78560,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1256},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"9d35f85f-29ac-406f-ac82-d85e2fdf7651","uuid":"7a4f4489-9538-4b0e-abb2-0f90fa933ce4","timestamp":"2026-07-27T08:23:58.071Z","request_id":"req_011CdSEtU9MTVcvCMUJ3Ww5X"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdSFCC6hfoK7hBwt42XMr","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01WoL6SUtifEQ58bmMeokZfr","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/testing-goal-001/2026-07-27T081521Z-claude-no-skill-3/workspace/FINDINGS.md","content":"# UsdtYieldVault — pre-deployment review\n\n**Verdict: do not ship this on Monday.**\n\nNot \"ship with caveats\". As written, `UsdtYieldVault` **cannot take a single deposit\nagainst the real USDT contract** — the happy path reverts on mainnet. And if that one\nline were fixed, the vault would still pay depositors back *less than they put in* after\na year in Aave, because it never accounts for the yield it exists to collect.\n\nSix findings below. Every one has a command you can run and the output I got.\n\n---\n\n## Why the 39 green tests didn't catch any of this\n\nThe suite is well-formed — clear names, good arrange/act/assert, no obvious gaps. The\nproblem isn't the tests, it's the two mocks they run against. Both are *simpler than the\nthings they stand in for*, and the entire risk of this contract lives in the difference:\n\n| Mock | What it does | What the real thing does |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `test/mocks/MockUSDT.sol` | Stock OpenZeppelin `ERC20`. `approve` returns `bool`. | Tether's `TetherToken` returns **nothing** from `approve`/`transfer`/`transferFrom`, has an approve-race guard, and has an owner-settable transfer fee. |\n| `test/mocks/MockAavePool.sol` | `MockAToken` is a plain ERC20. A supplied balance **never changes**. | aUSDT balances **grow every block**. That growth is the product. |\n\nBecause the mock aToken never accrues, no test in the suite can distinguish \"the vault\ncorrectly tracks its Aave position\" from \"the vault ignores its Aave position entirely.\"\nThe vault does the second thing. `forge coverage` reports 100% because coverage measures\nwhich lines *ran*, not which behaviours were *asserted* — every line of `deposit()` runs\nfine in a world where USDT returns a bool and interest doesn't exist.\n\nWorth noting on its own: the `aUsdt` immutable is written in the constructor and then\n**never read anywhere in the contract**.\n\n```\n$ grep -n \"aUsdt\" src/UsdtYieldVault.sol\n41:    IERC20 public immutable aUsdt;\n68:    /// @param _aUsdt The Aave aUSDT receipt token.\n72:    constructor(address _usdt, address _aUsdt, address _aavePool, uint256 _depositFeeBps, address initialOwner)\n76:        aUsdt = IERC20(_aUsdt);\n```\n\nThe vault stores a pointer to the only on-chain source of truth about what it actually\nowns, and never asks it. That single fact is the root cause of findings F2 and F3.\n\n---\n\n## Reproducing\n\nNothing under `src/`, `test/UsdtYieldVault.t.sol`, or `test/mocks/` was modified. Confirm with:\n\n```\n$ git status --short src test/UsdtYieldVault.t.sol test/mocks\n```\n\nNew files, all additive:\n\n| File | Purpose |\n| --- | --- |\n| `test/MainnetFork.t.sol` | Runs the vault against the **actual deployed bytecode** at the three README addresses. |\n| `test/helpers/RealisticMocks.sol` | A USDT stand-in with Tether's real ABI quirks; an Aave pool whose aToken actually accrues. |\n| `test/RealUsdtBehavior.t.sol` | F1, F6 — offline, no network needed. |\n| `test/YieldAccrual.t.sol` | F2. |\n| `test/FeeAccounting.t.sol` | F3 — uses the project's **own** mocks, so nothing here can be blamed on my harness. |\n| `test/OwnerPowers.t.sol` | F4, F5 — also uses the project's own mocks. |\n| `test/VaultInvariants.t.sol` | Property tests over random deposit/withdraw sequences. |\n\nThe tests are written to **assert the correct behaviour**, so a failure is the bug. All\nexcept `test/MainnetFork.t.sol` are offline. The fork tests default to a public RPC and\nare pinned to block 21,000,000; override with `MAINNET_RPC_URL` if that endpoint is\nrate-limiting you.\n\nBaseline first — the existing suite is untouched and still green:\n\n```\n$ forge test --match-path \"test/UsdtYieldVault.t.sol\"\n[PASS] test_WithdrawFeeBps() (gas: 5540)\n[PASS] test_WithdrawReturnsUsdt() (gas: 196362)\nSuite result: ok. 39 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 10.36ms (19.57ms CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 164.12ms (10.36ms CPU time): 39 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (39 total tests)\n```\n\n---\n\n# F1 — CRITICAL: `deposit()` reverts against the real USDT. The vault is inoperable on mainnet.\n\n**Where:** `src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:94`\n\n```solidity\nusdt.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);\nusdt.approve(address(aavePool), amount);   // <-- line 94, raw IERC20 call\n```\n\nLine 93 uses `SafeERC20`, which tolerates a token that returns no data. Line 94 calls\n`approve` **through the raw `IERC20` interface**, which is declared `returns (bool)`.\nSolidity therefore emits a `returndatasize() >= 32` check after the call. USDT returns\n**zero bytes**. The check fails and the whole transaction reverts.\n\nThere is no configuration, no fee setting, and no deposit size that avoids this. Every\ndeposit fails, always, for everyone.\n\n### Evidence — against the deployed contract at `0xdAC17F9…`\n\n```\n$ MAINNET_RPC_URL=https://eth.drpc.org forge test --match-path \"test/MainnetFork.t.sol\" -vv\nRan 3 tests for test/MainnetFork.t.sol:MainnetForkTest\n[FAIL: EvmError: Revert] test_F1_DepositWorksAgainstRealUsdt() (gas: 97905)\n[FAIL: real USDT must return 32 bytes for IERC20.approve to decode: 0 != 32] test_F1_RawApproveOnRealUsdtDecodesAsBool() (gas: 37161)\nLogs:\n  low-level call succeeded: true\n  returndata length: 0\n\n[PASS] test_F2_RealAaveAccruesInterestOnASuppliedBalance() (gas: 353276)\nLogs:\n  aUSDT at supply time : 1000000000\n  aUSDT after 365 days : 1042571282\n  interest accrued     : 42571282\n\nSuite result: FAILED. 1 passed; 2 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 368.81ms (1.27ms CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 370.05ms (368.81ms CPU time): 1 tests passed, 2 failed, 0 skipped (3 total tests)\n```\n\nNote `low-level call succeeded: true` with `returndata length: 0` — USDT's `approve`\n*works*, it just doesn't return the bool the vault's interface insists on.\n\nThe trace shows exactly where it dies — `transferFrom` succeeds, `approve` succeeds and\nreturns `[Stop]` (no data), and the vault reverts before ever reaching `aavePool.supply`:\n\n```\n$ MAINNET_RPC_URL=https://eth.drpc.org forge test --match-test test_F1_DepositWorksAgainstRealUsdt -vvvv\n  [97905] MainnetForkTest::test_F1_DepositWorksAgainstRealUsdt()\n    ├─ [5031] 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7::balanceOf(alice: [0x328809Bc894f92807417D2dAD6b7C998c1aFdac6]) [staticcall]\n    │   └─ ← [Return] 100000000000 [1e11]\n    ├─ [3356] 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7::allowance(alice: [0x328809Bc894f92807417D2dAD6b7C998c1aFdac6], UsdtYieldVault: [0x5615dEB798BB3E4dFa0139dFa1b3D433Cc23b72f]) [staticcall]\n    │   └─ ← [Return] 115792089237316195423570985008687907853269984665640564039457584007913129639935 [1.157e77]\n    ├─ [0] VM::prank(alice: [0x328809Bc894f92807417D2dAD6b7C998c1aFdac6])\n    │   └─ ← [Return]\n    ├─ [75674] UsdtYieldVault::deposit(1000000000 [1e9])\n    │   ├─ [37630] 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7::transferFrom(alice: [0x328809Bc894f92807417D2dAD6b7C998c1aFdac6], UsdtYieldVault: [0x5615dEB798BB3E4dFa0139dFa1b3D433Cc23b72f], 1000000000 [1e9])\n    │   │   ├─ emit Transfer(from: alice: [0x328809Bc894f92807417D2dAD6b7C998c1aFdac6], to: UsdtYieldVault: [0x5615dEB798BB3E4dFa0139dFa1b3D433Cc23b72f], value: 1000000000 [1e9])\n    │   │   └─ ← [Stop]\n    │   ├─ [24953] 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7::approve(0x87870Bca3F3fD6335C3F4ce8392D69350B4fA4E2, 1000000000 [1e9])\n    │   │   ├─ emit Approval(owner: UsdtYieldVault: [0x5615dEB798BB3E4dFa0139dFa1b3D433Cc23b72f], spender: 0x87870Bca3F3fD6335C3F4ce8392D69350B4fA4E2, value: 1000000000 [1e9])\n    │   │   └─ ← [Stop]\n    │   └─ ← [Revert] EvmError: Revert\n    └─ ← [Revert] EvmError: Revert\n\nBacktrace:\n  at UsdtYieldVault.deposit\n  at MainnetForkTest.test_F1_DepositWorksAgainstRealUsdt\n```\n\n### Evidence — offline, no RPC needed\n\nSame test as the suite's `test_DepositMintsShares`, with only the token swapped:\n\n```\n$ forge test --match-path \"test/RealUsdtBehavior.t.sol\" -vv\nRan 3 tests for test/RealUsdtBehavior.t.sol:RealUsdtBehaviorTest\n[FAIL: EvmError: Revert] test_F1_DepositMintsShares() (gas: 87180)\n[FAIL: IERC20.approve requires 32 bytes of returndata to decode: 0 != 32] test_F1_SafeErc20HandlesUsdtButRawApproveDoesNot() (gas: 80253)\nLogs:\n  approve call succeeded: true\n  approve returndata length: 0\n\n[FAIL: vault books `amount`, so it must receive `amount`: 999000000 != 1000000000] test_F6_DepositCreditsOnlyWhatWasActuallyReceived() (gas: 121899)\nLogs:\n  amount alice sent      : 1000000000\n  amount vault received  : 999000000\n  amount vault would book: 1000000000\n\nSuite result: FAILED. 0 passed; 3 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 2.39ms (3.77ms CPU time)\n```\n\n### Fix\n\nReplace the raw approve on line 94 with `SafeERC20`'s, which handles both the missing\nreturn value and USDT's non-zero-to-non-zero approve guard (`forceApprove` is available\nin the OZ 5.6.1 already vendored in `lib/`):\n\n```solidity\nusdt.forceApprove(address(aavePool), amount);\n```\n\nThen set the allowance back to zero after `supply` returns, so a partially-consumed\nallowance can never wedge the *next* deposit on USDT's approve-race guard. A cleaner\nalternative is a one-time `forceApprove(pool, type(uint256).max)` in the constructor,\ndropping the per-deposit approve entirely.\n\n**Also add a CI check that this class of bug can't come back:** the only reason it\nsurvived to a ship-ready state is that `MockUSDT` is a stock ERC20. Point the existing\nsuite at a USDT-faithful mock (`test/helpers/RealisticMocks.sol:RealUsdt` is one), or\nadd a forked-mainnet smoke test to CI.\n\n---\n\n# F2 — CRITICAL: the yield vault does not account for yield. Depositors lose money.\n\n**Where:** `src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:143-145`, and the absence of any accrual path.\n\n```solidity\nfunction totalAssets() public view returns (uint256) {\n    return totalAssetsStored;   // a stored number, not a measured one\n}\n```\n\n`totalAssetsStored` only ever moves inside `deposit()` and `withdraw()`. Interest paid by\nAave into the vault's aUSDT balance is never read, never accrued, and never distributed —\nthe contract has no `harvest`, no `sync`, no `accrue`, and never calls\n`aUsdt.balanceOf(address(this))` at all.\n\nConsequences, in order of severity:\n\n1. **Share price is permanently flat.** The vault is functionally a zero-yield custodian.\n2. **Depositors are net negative.** They pay 10 bps in and 30 bps out for 0% return.\n3. **The interest is unrecoverable.** Once everyone exits, `totalShares == 0`, so no share\n   can ever claim the accumulated aUSDT — and there is no owner sweep or rescue function.\n   It is not \"unclaimed\". It is **destroyed**.\n\nThat Aave really does pay this interest is confirmed on the fork against the live pool\n(`test_F2_RealAaveAccruesInterestOnASuppliedBalance`, above): 1,000 USDT → 1,042.57 USDT\nover 365 days at block 21,000,000's rate. The local test uses a flat 5% for round numbers.\n\n### Evidence\n\n```\n$ forge test --match-path \"test/YieldAccrual.t.sol\" -vv\nRan 5 tests for test/YieldAccrual.t.sol:YieldAccrualTest\n[FAIL: after a year at 5% APY the depositor should be up, not down: 997000000 <= 1000000000] test_F2_DepositorEarnsTheYield() (gas: 239828)\nLogs:\n  alice deposited          : 1000000000\n  aUSDT the vault earned   : 1050000000\n  alice received back      : 997000000\n  net P/L for alice        : -3000000\n\n[FAIL: a year of 5% APY on 1,000 USDT must show up in the holder's claim: 1000500250 < 1040000000] test_F2_EarlyDepositorsClaimReflectsTheYieldTheyEarned() (gas: 320179)\nLogs:\n  alice shares (deposited at t=0, held one year)  : 999000000000000000000\n  bob shares   (deposited at t=1y, held nothing)  : 998001000000000000000\n  alice claim  : 1000500250\n  bob claim    : 999499749\n  alice premium over bob : 1000501\n\n[FAIL: no USDT may be left behind with zero shares outstanding to claim it: 53000000 != 0] test_F2_InterestIsNotStrandedAfterFullExit() (gas: 241492)\nLogs:\n  totalShares after full exit : 0\n  totalAssetsStored           : 0\n  aUSDT still held by vault   : 53000000\n\n[FAIL: a yield vault's share price must rise as interest accrues: 1001001 <= 1001001] test_F2_SharePriceRisesWithYield() (gas: 220912)\nLogs:\n  sharePrice at deposit    : 1001001\n  sharePrice one year later: 1001001\n\n[FAIL: totalAssets() must reflect the vault's real Aave position: 1000000000 != 1050000000] test_F2_TotalAssetsTracksTheAavePosition() (gas: 223558)\nLogs:\n  aUSDT actually held by vault : 1050000000\n  vault.totalAssets()          : 1000000000\n  unaccounted interest         : 50000000\n\nSuite result: FAILED. 0 passed; 5 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 1.73ms (3.98ms CPU time)\n```\n\nRead `test_F2_DepositorEarnsTheYield` closely, because it is the whole product in five\nlines. Alice deposits **1,000 USDT**. The vault's Aave position grows to **1,050**. Alice\nwithdraws and receives **997**. She is down **3 USDT** after a year of lending at 5%, and\nthe 53 USDT she earned is gone.\n\n`test_F2_SharePriceRisesWithYield` is the cleanest single artefact: `1001001` before a\nyear passes, `1001001` after.\n\n### Fix\n\nMake `totalAssets()` **measure** rather than remember:\n\n```solidity\nfunction totalAssets() public view returns (uint256) {\n    return aUsdt.balanceOf(address(this));\n}\n```\n\naUSDT is rebasing — its `balanceOf` already equals the underlying USDT redeemable — so\nthis is the correct source of truth and makes the `aUsdt` immutable earn its place. Then:\n\n- delete `totalAssetsStored` and every write to it, and have `convertToShares` /\n  `convertToAssets` / `sharePrice` read `totalAssets()`;\n- in `withdraw`, take the fee out of `netAssets` explicitly and leave it in Aave, where the\n  balance-based `totalAssets()` now correctly attributes it to the remaining holders\n  (this also fixes F3);\n- because `totalAssets()` becomes externally influenceable by a direct aUSDT transfer,\n  add the standard ERC-4626 inflation-attack defence — virtual shares/assets, or a dead\n  first-deposit — before going live. `MIN_DEPOSIT` alone is not sufficient.\n\nThe bigger recommendation: this contract is re-deriving ERC-4626 and getting the derivation\nwrong. Inheriting OpenZeppelin's `ERC4626` and overriding `totalAssets()` would eliminate\nF2 and F3 by construction, and give you a transferable share token for free.\n\n---\n\n# F3 — HIGH: the 30 bps withdrawal fee accrues to nobody. It is burned.\n\n**Where:** `src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:112-119`\n\n```solidity\nuint256 fee = (grossAssets * WITHDRAW_FEE_BPS) / BPS_DENOMINATOR;\nnetAssets = grossAssets - fee;\n...\ntotalAssetsStored -= grossAssets;             // books drop by GROSS\naavePool.withdraw(address(usdt), netAssets, msg.sender);   // but only NET leaves Aave\n```\n\nThe fee stays in Aave — but the books are debited the gross, so the fee is subtracted from\nthe tracked assets at the same moment. Share price is mathematically unchanged by a\nwithdrawal. Both `README.md` and the contract's own `@dev` header state:\n\n> \"Both fees stay supplied in Aave and accrue to the remaining shareholders rather than\n> being swept to the owner.\"\n\nHalf of that is true. The **deposit** fee does accrue exactly as documented — I've included\na passing test proving it, so this finding is a real asymmetry and not a misreading of the\ndesign. The **withdrawal** fee does not.\n\n### Evidence — using the project's own mocks\n\n```\n$ forge test --match-path \"test/FeeAccounting.t.sol\" -vv\nRan 4 tests for test/FeeAccounting.t.sol:FeeAccountingTest\n[FAIL: every aUSDT the vault holds must be backed by a share claim: 1000500251 != 1003498750] test_F3_BooksMatchTheAavePosition() (gas: 350615)\nLogs:\n  aUSDT held by vault : 1003498750\n  vault.totalAssets() : 1000500251\n  unowned difference  : 2998499\n\n[PASS] test_F3_DepositFeeDoesAccrueAsDocumented() (gas: 261536)\nLogs:\n  alice claim before bob's deposit : 1000000000\n  alice claim after bob's deposit  : 1000500250\n\n[FAIL: normal use must not accumulate unclaimable balances: 59941160 != 0] test_F3_LeakDoesNotCompoundOverManyCycles() (gas: 2275735)\nLogs:\n  unowned aUSDT after 20 deposit/withdraw cycles : 59941160\n\n[FAIL: the fee bob paid must accrue to alice, the only remaining shareholder: 1 !~= 2998499 (max delta: 2, real delta: 2998498)] test_F3_WithdrawFeeAccruesToRemainingShareholders() (gas: 351647)\nLogs:\n  bob withdrew (net)        : 996501250\n  alice claim before        : 1000500250\n  alice claim after         : 1000500251\n  alice gained              : 1\n  withdrawal fee bob paid   : 2998499\n\nSuite result: FAILED. 1 passed; 3 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 1.69ms (1.70ms CPU time)\n```\n\nBob pays a **2.998499 USDT** withdrawal fee. Alice, the only remaining shareholder and\ntherefore the sole intended beneficiary, gains **1 base unit — 0.000001 USDT**. That single\nunit is rounding dust, not the fee.\n\n### Evidence — it compounds under normal use\n\nThis is not a rounding curiosity. It leaks on *every* exit and never comes back. Over 20\nordinary deposit/withdraw cycles the vault accumulates **59.94 USDT** that no share can\nclaim.\n\nThe invariant run makes the scale clear. Random deposit/withdraw sequences from three\nactors, deterministic seed:\n\n```\n$ forge test --match-test \"invariant_EveryHeldAssetIsBackedByAShare|invariant_CallSummary\" --fuzz-seed 1 -vv\nRan 2 tests for test/VaultInvariants.t.sol:VaultInvariantsTest\n[PASS] invariant_CallSummary() (runs: 256, calls: 128000, reverts: 0)\n\n╭--------------+----------+-------+---------+----------╮\n| Contract     | Selector | Calls | Reverts | Discards |\n+======================================================+\n| VaultHandler | deposit  | 64271 | 0       | 0        |\n|--------------+----------+-------+---------+----------|\n| VaultHandler | withdraw | 63729 | 0       | 0        |\n╰--------------+----------+-------+---------+----------╯\n\nLogs:\n  deposit calls    : 248\n  withdraw calls   : 249\n  aUSDT held       : 40206448852\n  totalAssetsStored: 35997477842\n  unclaimable      : 4208971010\n\n[FAIL: vault holds aUSDT that no share can claim: 18298360711 != 18278952688]\n\t[Sequence] (original: 9, shrunk: 2)\n\t\tsender=0x000000000000000000000000000000001554d114 addr=[test/VaultInvariants.t.sol:VaultHandler]0x5991A2dF15A8F6A256D3Ec51E99254Cd3fb576A9 calldata=deposit(uint256,uint256) args=[1673, 94]\n\t\tsender=0x3790Bf7753a8ec3905c4D0937C7c0d59dE0EA17b addr=[test/VaultInvariants.t.sol:VaultHandler]0x5991A2dF15A8F6A256D3Ec51E99254Cd3fb576A9 calldata=withdraw(uint256,uint256) args=[11301594005382832122848177774449925492119437927319565579473933979 [1.13e64], 1066237421792316739298199530987255338825 [1.066e39]]\n invariant_EveryHeldAssetIsBackedByAShare() (runs: 0, calls: 0, reverts: 0)\n```\n\nAfter ~497 successful operations: **4,208 USDT unclaimable against 35,997 USDT booked —\n11.7% of the vault**. It shrinks to a two-call counterexample: one deposit, one withdrawal.\n(Invariant fuzzing is seed-dependent; `--fuzz-seed 1` reproduces these exact numbers. Any\nseed fails, with different figures.)\n\n### Fix\n\nDebit the books by what actually left, and leave the fee behind as a genuine credit to the\nremaining holders:\n\n```solidity\ntotalAssetsStored -= netAssets;   // not grossAssets\n```\n\nThis is correct only while shares outstanding are non-zero. If the last holder exits, the\nfee they just paid is stranded again — so also make the final withdrawal fee-exempt, or\nadopt the balance-based `totalAssets()` from F2, which handles both cases correctly and\nmakes this line disappear along with `totalAssetsStored` itself.\n\n---\n\n# F4 — HIGH: `setDepositFee` is unbounded. The owner can take depositors' principal.\n\n**Where:** `src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:126-130`\n\n```solidity\nfunction setDepositFee(uint256 newFeeBps) external onlyOwner {\n    depositFeeBps = newFeeBps;   // no cap, no timelock, effective immediately\n}\n```\n\nNo upper bound is checked anywhere. The existing suite tests that the setter stores a value\nand that non-owners are rejected — it never asks *which* values the owner may store.\n\nTwo distinct problems:\n\n**Denial of service.** Any value above 10,000 makes `amount - fee` on line 88 underflow.\nDeposits revert with a panic, permanently, until the owner relents.\n\n**Theft.** Because the deposit fee legitimately accrues to existing shareholders (F3), an\nowner holding shares can raise the fee and have depositors' money routed into their own\nposition. There is no timelock, so the new fee applies to the very next transaction — a\ndepositor cannot see the `DepositFeeUpdated` event and react in time, and the owner can\nsandwich a pending deposit in a single block.\n\n### Evidence\n\n```\n$ forge test --match-path \"test/OwnerPowers.t.sol\" -vv\nRan 5 tests for test/OwnerPowers.t.sol:OwnerPowersTest\n[FAIL: fee must never exceed 100%: 20000 > 10000] test_F4_DepositFeeIsCappedAtOneHundredPercent() (gas: 21370)\n[FAIL: panic: arithmetic underflow or overflow (0x11)] test_F4_DepositStillWorksAfterAnyAcceptedFee() (gas: 27766)\n[FAIL: the owner must not be able to capture depositor principal: 18918918918 > 1100000000] test_F4_OwnerCannotDrainDepositorsByRaisingTheFee() (gas: 438261)\nLogs:\n  owner deposited        : 1000000000\n  owner claim afterwards : 18918918918\n  owner profit           : 17918918918\n  alice deposited 10,000, claim now : 1891891891\n  bob   deposited 10,000, claim now : 189189189\n  owner shares: 999000000000000000000\n\n[FAIL: a renounced owner must not leave funds frozen forever] test_F5_PauseIsNotPermanentlyLockableByOwner() (gas: 250316)\nLogs:\n  owner after renounce : 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000\n  paused               : true\n\n[FAIL: EnforcedPause()] test_F5_PausedVaultStillAllowsWithdrawals() (gas: 238238)\nSuite result: FAILED. 0 passed; 5 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 1.39ms (2.19ms CPU time)\n```\n\nThe drain scenario, in the owner's favour and entirely within the rules as written:\n\n| Party | Deposited | Claim afterwards |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| owner | 1,000 | **18,918.92** |\n| alice | 10,000 | 1,891.89 |\n| bob | 10,000 | 189.19 |\n\nThe owner turns 1,000 USDT into a claim on 18,918 — a **17,918 USDT profit** taken directly\nfrom Alice and Bob's principal. Alice recovers 19% of her deposit; Bob recovers 1.9%.\n\nWhether or not you trust the key holder, this is a power an auditor will flag and a\ndepositor will discover. It should not exist.\n\n### Fix\n\nCap the fee at a value depositors can rely on, and enforce it in the setter:\n\n```solidity\nuint256 public constant MAX_DEPOSIT_FEE_BPS = 100; // 1%\n\nfunction setDepositFee(uint256 newFeeBps) external onlyOwner {\n    if (newFeeBps > MAX_DEPOSIT_FEE_BPS) revert FeeTooHigh();\n    ...\n}\n```\n\nAdditionally: put the owner behind a multisig with a timelock on `setDepositFee`, so a fee\nchange is announced before it can be applied. A cap alone still lets a single EOA move the\nfee to the cap without warning.\n\n---\n\n# F5 — MEDIUM: `pause()` locks depositors out of their own funds, and can be made permanent.\n\n**Where:** `src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:107` — `withdraw` carries `whenNotPaused`.\n\nA pause should stop the vault taking on *new* risk. This one also stops existing depositors\nfrom leaving. There is no emergency-exit path that bypasses the pause, no timelock on\n`unpause`, and no maximum pause duration.\n\nWorse, `Ownable` exposes `renounceOwnership()`. Pause, then renounce, and the vault is\nfrozen with every depositor's funds inside it and no address on earth able to unpause. The\n`test_F5_PauseIsNotPermanentlyLockableByOwner` output above shows the end state: owner\n`0x0000…0000`, `paused: true`, and Alice's `withdraw` reverting with `EnforcedPause()`.\n\nThis need not be malicious — a lost or compromised owner key reaches the same place.\n\n### Fix\n\n- Drop `whenNotPaused` from `withdraw`. Depositors should always be able to exit; if the\n  concern is a bank run, that is what a pause on `deposit` is for.\n- If withdrawals genuinely must be pausable, add an emergency-withdraw path that ignores\n  the pause, or a maximum pause duration after which anyone may call `unpause`.\n- Override `renounceOwnership()` to revert, and use `Ownable2Step` so ownership cannot be\n  transferred to an address that does not confirm.\n\n---\n\n# F6 — MEDIUM (latent): a USDT transfer fee would silently break deposit accounting.\n\n**Where:** `src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:93-97`\n\nThe vault credits `totalAssetsStored += amount` and supplies `amount` to Aave, assuming the\n`transferFrom` delivered exactly `amount`. USDT's deployed bytecode contains\n`basisPointsRate`, `maximumFee`, and an owner-only `setParams` that can turn a transfer fee\non. It is 0 today. It is not guaranteed to stay 0, and this vault is meant to hold real\nmoney indefinitely.\n\nIf Tether sets it, deposits either revert (the vault tries to supply more than it received)\nor, if the vault happens to hold a stray balance, over-credit the depositor — which under\nthe F3 accounting would come out of everyone else's claim.\n\n### Evidence\n\nFrom the `test/RealUsdtBehavior.t.sol` run above. With a 10 bps transfer fee set via the\nsame `setParams` signature the live token exposes:\n\n```\n[FAIL: vault books `amount`, so it must receive `amount`: 999000000 != 1000000000] test_F6_DepositCreditsOnlyWhatWasActuallyReceived() (gas: 121899)\nLogs:\n  amount alice sent      : 1000000000\n  amount vault received  : 999000000\n  amount vault would book: 1000000000\n```\n\nThe depositor sends 1,000 USDT, the vault receives 999, and books 1,000.\n\n### Fix\n\nMeasure the delta rather than trusting the argument:\n\n```solidity\nuint256 balanceBefore = usdt.balanceOf(address(this));\nusdt.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);\nuint256 received = usdt.balanceOf(address(this)) - balanceBefore;\n```\n\nThen compute shares, the approve, the `supply`, and the `totalAssetsStored` credit from\n`received`. Note this must be done *before* `convertToShares`, since the fee changes how\nmany shares the deposit is worth.\n\n---\n\n## What I checked that holds up\n\nReporting these too, since they bound the severity of the above.\n\n**The vault is never insolvent, and share accounting is self-consistent.** Both pass across\n256 runs × 128,000 calls:\n\n```\n[PASS] invariant_ShareBalancesSumToTotalShares() (runs: 256, calls: 128000, reverts: 0)\n[PASS] invariant_VaultIsNeverInsolvent() (runs: 256, calls: 128000, reverts: 0)\n```\n\nThis matters: the F2/F3 drift runs in the *safe* direction. The vault always holds at least\nwhat its books claim, so no user can withdraw another user's principal through the\naccounting bugs — value gets stranded, not stolen. F4 is the one path by which a party\ntakes value from another, and it requires the owner key.\n\nAlso checked and found sound: `nonReentrant` is correctly applied to both state-changing\nentry points and state is written before the external call in `withdraw`; the\n`totalAssetsStored -= grossAssets` subtraction cannot underflow, since `convertToAssets`\nfloors and is bounded above by the stored total; `convertToShares` / `convertToAssets`\nround down consistently, in the vault's favour; and the `totalShares > 0 && totalAssetsStored == 0`\ndivision-by-zero state was not reachable in 128,000 fuzzed operations.\n\nI did **not** verify: behaviour when the Aave USDT reserve is frozen, paused, or short of\nliquidity (`withdraw` would revert and there is no fallback path); the deployment script and\nconstructor arguments, since there is no deploy script in the repo; or the aUSDT address in\nthe README against Aave's registry at current head.\n\n---\n\n## Bottom line\n\n| # | Severity | Finding | Ships Monday? |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| F1 | Critical | `deposit()` reverts against real USDT — vault inoperable | Blocker |\n| F2 | Critical | Yield never accrues; depositors net negative; interest destroyed | Blocker |\n| F3 | High | Withdrawal fee accrues to nobody; ~11% of TVL unclaimable in simulation | Blocker |\n| F4 | High | Unbounded deposit fee lets the owner take depositor principal | Blocker |\n| F5 | Medium | Pause traps depositor funds; can be made permanent | Fix before launch |\n| F6 | Medium | Latent USDT transfer-fee incompatibility | Fix before launch |\n\nF1 is trivially fixable — one line. F2 and F3 are not: they are a design error in how the\ncontract represents its own position, and correcting them changes the share-price maths,\nwhich reopens inflation-attack questions that also need answering. That is not a weekend's\nwork, and it needs an external audit afterward rather than a re-run of the suite.\n\nThe most useful thing I can tell you is not any single finding but the shape of them: the\n39 tests all pass, and they would still all pass with every one of these bugs present,\nbecause they only ever test the vault against a world that is simpler than mainnet. Before\nthis ships, the mocks need to be at least as adversarial as the contracts you are actually\nintegrating with, and the suite needs invariants — statements about what must always be\ntrue — rather than only example-based assertions about specific numbers.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":868,"cache_read_input_tokens":97029,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":868},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"9d35f85f-29ac-406f-ac82-d85e2fdf7651","uuid":"d4f1361a-b078-43dd-a10d-5a89a695ffe7","timestamp":"2026-07-27T08:30:04.091Z","request_id":"req_011CdSFC8nXTWxKdCUQVDHRv"}

As written, `UsdtYieldVault` **cannot take a single deposit\nagainst the real USDT contract** — the happy path reverts on mainnet. And if that one\nline were fixed, the vault would still pay depositors back *less than they put in* after\na year in Aave, because it never accounts for the yield it exists to collect.\n\nSix findings below. Every one has a command you can run and the output I got.\n\n---\n\n## Why the 39 green tests didn't catch any of this\n\nThe suite is well-formed — clear names, good arrange/act/assert, no obvious gaps. The\nproblem isn't the tests, it's the two mocks they run against. Both are *simpler than the\nthings they stand in for*, and the entire risk of this contract lives in the difference:\n\n| Mock | What it does | What the real thing does |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `test/mocks/MockUSDT.sol` | Stock OpenZeppelin `ERC20`. `approve` returns `bool`. | Tether's `TetherToken` returns **nothing** from `approve`/`transfer`/`transferFrom`, has an approve-race guard, and has an owner-settable transfer fee. |\n| `test/mocks/MockAavePool.sol` | `MockAToken` is a plain ERC20. A supplied balance **never changes**. | aUSDT balances **grow every block**. That growth is the product. |\n\nBecause the mock aToken never accrues, no test in the suite can distinguish \"the vault\ncorrectly tracks its Aave position\" from \"the vault ignores its Aave position entirely.\"\nThe vault does the second thing. `forge coverage` reports 100% because coverage measures\nwhich lines *ran*, not which behaviours were *asserted* — every line of `deposit()` runs\nfine in a world where USDT returns a bool and interest doesn't exist.\n\nWorth noting on its own: the `aUsdt` immutable is written in the constructor and then\n**never read anywhere in the contract**.\n\n```\n$ grep -n \"aUsdt\" src/UsdtYieldVault.sol\n41:    IERC20 public immutable aUsdt;\n68:    /// @param _aUsdt The Aave aUSDT receipt token.\n72:    constructor(address _usdt, address _aUsdt, address _aavePool, uint256 _depositFeeBps, address initialOwner)\n76:        aUsdt = IERC20(_aUsdt);\n```\n\nThe vault stores a pointer to the only on-chain source of truth about what it actually\nowns, and never asks it. That single fact is the root cause of findings F2 and F3.\n\n---\n\n## Reproducing\n\nNothing under `src/`, `test/UsdtYieldVault.t.sol`, or `test/mocks/` was modified. Confirm with:\n\n```\n$ git status --short src test/UsdtYieldVault.t.sol test/mocks\n```\n\nNew files, all additive:\n\n| File | Purpose |\n| --- | --- |\n| `test/MainnetFork.t.sol` | Runs the vault against the **actual deployed bytecode** at the three README addresses. |\n| `test/helpers/RealisticMocks.sol` | A USDT stand-in with Tether's real ABI quirks; an Aave pool whose aToken actually accrues. |\n| `test/RealUsdtBehavior.t.sol` | F1, F6 — offline, no network needed. |\n| `test/YieldAccrual.t.sol` | F2. |\n| `test/FeeAccounting.t.sol` | F3 — uses the project's **own** mocks, so nothing here can be blamed on my harness. |\n| `test/OwnerPowers.t.sol` | F4, F5 — also uses the project's own mocks. |\n| `test/VaultInvariants.t.sol` | Property tests over random deposit/withdraw sequences. |\n\nThe tests are written to **assert the correct behaviour**, so a failure is the bug. All\nexcept `test/MainnetFork.t.sol` are offline. The fork tests default to a public RPC and\nare pinned to block 21,000,000; override with `MAINNET_RPC_URL` if that endpoint is\nrate-limiting you.\n\nBaseline first — the existing suite is untouched and still green:\n\n```\n$ forge test --match-path \"test/UsdtYieldVault.t.sol\"\n[PASS] test_WithdrawFeeBps() (gas: 5540)\n[PASS] test_WithdrawReturnsUsdt() (gas: 196362)\nSuite result: ok. 39 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 10.36ms (19.57ms CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 164.12ms (10.36ms CPU time): 39 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (39 total tests)\n```\n\n---\n\n# F1 — CRITICAL: `deposit()` reverts against the real USDT. The vault is inoperable on mainnet.\n\n**Where:** `src/UsdtYieldVault.sol:94`\n\n```solidity\nusdt.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);\nusdt.approve(address(aavePool), amount);   // <-- line 94, raw IERC20 call\n```\n\nLine 93 uses `SafeERC20`, which tolerates a token that returns no data. Line 94 calls\n`approve` **through the raw `IERC20` interface**, which is declared `returns (bool)`.\nSolidity therefore emits a `returndatasize() >= 32` check after the call. USDT returns\n**zero bytes**. The check fails and the whole transaction reverts.\n\nThere is no configuration, no fee setting, and no deposit size that avoids this. Every\ndeposit fails, always, for everyone.\n\n### Evidence — against the deployed contract at `0xdAC17F9…`\n\n```\n$ MAINNET_RPC_URL=https://eth.drpc.org forge test --match-path \"test/MainnetFork.t.sol\" -vv\nRan 3 tests for test/MainnetFork.t.sol:MainnetForkTest\n[FAIL: EvmError: Revert] test_F1_DepositWorksAgainstRealUsdt() (gas: 97905)\n[FAIL: real USDT must return 32 bytes for IERC20.approve to decode: 0 != 32] test_F1_RawApproveOnRealUsdtDecodesAsBool() (gas: 37161)\nLogs:\n  low-level call succeeded: true\n  returndata length: 0\n\n[PASS] test_F2_RealAaveAccruesInterestOnASuppliedBalance() (gas: 353276)\nLogs:\n  aUSDT at supply time : 1000000000\n  aUSDT after 365 days : 1042571282\n  interest accrued     : 42571282\n\nSuite result: FAILED. 1 passed; 2 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 368.81ms (1.27ms CPU time)\n\nRan 1 test suite in 370.05ms (368.81ms CPU time): 1 tests passed, 2 failed, 0 skipped (3 total tests)\n```\n\nNote `low-level call succeeded: true` with `returndata length: 0` — USDT's `approve`\n*works*, it just doesn't return the bool the vault's interface insists on.\n\nThe trace shows exactly where it dies — `transferFrom` succeeds, `approve` succeeds and\nreturns `[Stop]` (no data), and the vault reverts before ever reaching `aavePool.supply`:\n\n```\n$ MAINNET_RPC_URL=https://eth.drpc.org forge test --match-test test_F1_DepositWorksAgainstRealUsdt -vvvv\n  [97905] MainnetForkTest::test_F1_DepositWorksAgainstRealUsdt()\n    ├─ [5031] 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7::balanceOf(alice: [0x328809Bc894f92807417D2dAD6b7C998c1aFdac6]) [staticcall]\n    │   └─ ← [Return] 100000000000 [1e11]\n    ├─ [3356] 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7::allowance(alice: [0x328809Bc894f92807417D2dAD6b7C998c1aFdac6], UsdtYieldVault: [0x5615dEB798BB3E4dFa0139dFa1b3D433Cc23b72f]) [staticcall]\n    │   └─ ← [Return] 115792089237316195423570985008687907853269984665640564039457584007913129639935 [1.157e77]\n    ├─ [0] VM::prank(alice: [0x328809Bc894f92807417D2dAD6b7C998c1aFdac6])\n    │   └─ ← [Return]\n    ├─ [75674] UsdtYieldVault::deposit(1000000000 [1e9])\n    │   ├─ [37630] 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7::transferFrom(alice: [0x328809Bc894f92807417D2dAD6b7C998c1aFdac6], UsdtYieldVault: [0x5615dEB798BB3E4dFa0139dFa1b3D433Cc23b72f], 1000000000 [1e9])\n    │   │   ├─ emit Transfer(from: alice: [0x328809Bc894f92807417D2dAD6b7C998c1aFdac6], to: UsdtYieldVault: [0x5615dEB798BB3E4dFa0139dFa1b3D433Cc23b72f], value: 1000000000 [1e9])\n    │   │   └─ ← [Stop]\n    │   ├─ [24953] 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7::approve(0x87870Bca3F3fD6335C3F4ce8392D69350B4fA4E2, 1000000000 [1e9])\n    │   │   ├─ emit Approval(owner: UsdtYieldVault:
